description: Programs captured from the C++-compiler-era tests/test_*.py modules, which asserted the C++ compiler's internals (its --offline option, --wasm-stats fields, goose.regions sections). Their subprocess calls were recorded with assertions disabled, and each unique source was run with plain upstream 32a4f44 (goose run and goose check, its own stdlib) at -O0, -O1 and -O2.

reasons.aliased-or-corrupt: Upstream reads aliased or corrupt bytes. In most of these a multiple-result return builds its first value over a returned local while a later value still reads that local, directly or through a reference or call; goose_spec.md section 7.3 (Named results) copies such a local instead, so the later value sees the local unchanged. In one, upstream writes an enum payload's field at one offset and reads it at another.
reasons.duplicate-contract: The same program as an existing upstream-differential fixture apart from its comments.
reasons.duplicate-fixture: Byte-identical to an existing fixture in tests/fixtures, whose own contracts already cover it.
reasons.host-import: Declares an extern function that only the old test's host supplied (prepared, callback, probe, forge, foreign, bench_input); plain upstream cannot link it, so it has no upstream output.
reasons.region-top-leftovers: Upstream shows region-top leftovers, layer 2 of the abandoned-destination bullet in docs/FEATURES.md: a cancelled exit's or cancelled append's bytes stay at the destination's start or region top, and a later return, push or append lands after them.
reasons.upstream-toolchain: Plain upstream's TinyCC rejects the C it generates ('constant exceeds 32 bit') for an array of about 6.1e18 elements or a pad of i64.max bytes, so upstream has no output; goose build with the system C compiler also fails.

gap_causes.fill-count-before-element: New: a fill [v; n] whose count the backend cannot hold aborts before v is evaluated, so the exit inside v is never taken (goose_spec.md section 4.2: v is evaluated once; section 2: evaluation is left to right). Direct Wasm traps "array repetition count out of range"; native C, building a whole assignment's fill in place, overflows its data stack first. Upstream evaluates v, takes its exit and prints 7.
gap_causes.limited-capacity-message: Open in docs/FEATURES.md (Differences found by the upstream differential run, the limited-capacity row): an overflowing runtime-capacity push reports "array capacity exceeded" on direct Wasm, where upstream and native C say "limited array capacity exceeded".
gap_causes.native-aggregate-memory-limit: New: the checker applies the direct-Wasm memory size (--wasm-max-pages, default 256 pages) to struct layouts on native C too, so a 400,000,000-byte struct is rejected ("aggregate layout exceeds configured memory"); upstream accepts it and runs it, and goose_spec.md section 10.4 sets the limit at 2^48 bytes.
gap_causes.wasm-named-result-alias: New: direct Wasm builds a multiple-result return over a returned local that a later result reads through a reference, so `return E.New { 0x0102030405060708 }, kept` gives 16909060 for kept where upstream and native C give 0 (goose_spec.md section 7.3, Named results: a returned local that another return's value may read is copied).
